newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-AJAX VICTORY IS "FANTASTIC RESULT" - VAN GAAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX VICTORY IS "FANTASTIC RESULT" - VAN GAAL.

text.p: Patrick Kluivert fired Ajax Amsterdam into the European Cup quarter-finals with the decisive goal in Wednesday's 1-0 win over Grasshopper Zurich, acclaimed by the Dutch team's coach Louis Van Gaal as a "fantastic result".
Needing nothing less than victory in their last Champions' League group A match to secure a place in the final eight for the third consecutive year, Ajax went on the attack right from the outset.
The Amsterdam club's persistence was rewarded in the 31st minute when Tijani Babangida spotted Kluivert unmarked near the penalty area.

Taking a perfect pass from the Nigerian winger, Kluivert blasted a low shot to the left corner past flat-footed goalkeeper Pascal Zuberbuehler, silencing most of a sell-out crowd of 22,000 that crammed into Hardturm stadium on a bitterly cold evening hoping to see Grasshopper qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time.
Grasshopper stormed onto the attack after the break but it was Ajax who enjoyed the better chances.
Kluivert looked to have his second only goal to watch his booming shot twist just wide of the post at the last second.
A few minutes later, Marc Overmars broke in alone on Zuberbueler and forced the Zurich keeper to come off his line to make a diving save.

But it was a crucial defensive effort by Overmars late in the match, kicking a point blank shot from Alexandre Comisetti off the line, that kept the Dutch club's hopes of a fifth European Cup title alive.

Having already been eliminated from the Dutch Cup and lying sixth in the league, Ajax's win -- their first in any competitiion in over a month -- helps to redeem what has otherwise been a disappointing season.
"This is a fantastic result for us," said Van Gaal. "After the winter break we will have a lot of our injured players back, and rest will help.
"The (European) Champions' Cup is the only thing we have to look forward too right now and we will place our attention on that."

Grasshopper: 1-Pascal Zuberbuehler, 3-Pascal Thueler, 4-Mats Gren, 6-Murat Yakin, 7-Antonio Esposito (Alexandre Comisetti 21st), 9-Viorel Moldovan, 10-Massimo Lombardo, 13-Georgios Nemtsoudis, 14-Johann Vogel (Joel Magnin 66th), 15-Nestor Subiat, 29-Boris Smiljanic.

Ajax Amsterdam: 1-Edwin Van der Sar, 2-John Veldman (Mario Melchiot 40th), 3-Frank de Boer, 6-Ronald De Boer, 7-Tijani Babangida (Nordin Wooter 84th), 9-Patrick Kluivert, 11-Marc Overmars, 14- Martijn Reuser (Jari Litmanen 63rd), 18-Kiki Musampa, 19-Arnold Scholten, 32-Arno Splinter.
